correctness.rationale: For \(Q=\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z\), the map \(H(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=(x_1-x_k,\ldots,x_{k-1}-x_k)\) is bijective on every one-coordinate slice. Composing it with a surjection onto the common range lets every fixed action reach every point of its prescribed neighborhood while the fallback intersection point keeps all outcomes inside that neighborhood. Thus the construction realizes exactly the original families with \(q\) copies each. In the one-neighborhood full-range frame, fixing one action leaves only the product of the other action counts, forcing that product to be at least \(r\) for every agent and hence \(\max_i d_i\ge q\). Fresh independent exhaustive slice checks for \(2\le k\le5\), \(1\le q\le4\) confirmed the critical combinatorial lemma.

originality.rationale: Ciardelli's complete constructive representation theorem was inspected at the definition, representability conditions and proof. Its construction gives each neighborhood a state-valued auxiliary label, hence a label set linear in the common range size. No inspected theorem optimizes those action multiplicities. Targeted Resultary searches in both game-semantic and slice-surjective/Latin-hypercube language found no prior root-size action bound or matching full-range lower obstruction. The combinatorial slice device itself is not claimed as new; originality is bounded to its sharp quantitative actual-effectivity application.

value.rationale: For three or more agents the theorem improves the constructive label factor from linear range size to the sharp root scale and proves that no uniformly smaller worst-case factor is possible. This is a natural quantitative refinement of a current representation theorem and can materially reduce concrete concurrent-game realizations.

limitations: Finite frames with at least two agents and deterministic concurrent-game realizations on the same state set.
The lower bound is worst-case rather than an exact per-frame minimum; for two agents the construction gives no root-scale improvement.
